item.title: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
item.description:
And it's more affordable than Nintendo's.

8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has announced the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's currently scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026.

Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99, it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Act Quick! Nintendo's Discounted Its Retro NSO Controllers For Black Friday (Europe)
item.description:
Put the class in classic.

Those who have long wanted to get their hands on Nintendo's classic range of NSO controllers are in luck, as the full collection has landed a special Black Friday discount on the European Nintendo Store.

And yes, we mean all of 'em. This means you can pick up the double NES controller pack for £34.99, the SNES pad for £18.89 (currently out of stock), the SEGA Mega Drive one for £27.99, and the N64 model for £27.99. Heck, even the Switch 2 GameCube controller has got a discount and now sits at a sweet £41.29.

item.title: GTA 6 Ties With Zelda: Ocarina Of Time As The Highest-Rated Game Ever
item.description:
"The greatest open world game".

Well folks, it's official: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are out, and it's currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (N64) as the highest-rated game ever on Metacritic.

There may yet be time for things to change as more reviews trickle in, but at the time of writing, GTA 6 is sitting at a remarkable 99 on the aggregate website, based on a total of 134 reviews.

item.title: Talking Point: As A Parent, What Worries You Most About Gaming?
item.description:
Nintendo's guide aims to highlight the benefits.

Over the summer, I replayed Ocarina of Time (1998) with my kids. I hadn't intended to, but it dawned on me that once the gorgeous remake landed, the original's visible polygons might not hold the same appeal for them. It was selfish, really, but I wanted them to experience the original magic as I did.

I held the pad but let them direct me, staying silent or feigning ignorance about puzzle solutions, letting them speculate and point out chests and switches I'd intentionally run past, involving them in an adventure they don't quite have the dexterity to control themselves.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Civilization Developer Firaxis Games Cuts A Third Of Its Staff, Studio Head Departs
item.description:
Grim.

A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Firaxis Games, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, has cut around one third of its staff. Meanwhile, its studio head Heather Hazen will also depart.

Approximately 60 people have been laid off as work on a new XCOM stalled over the Summer, with the game reportedly missing a huge milestone. Development will continue, but it will likely be met with a pretty drastic shake-up.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: "Pressure To Go For The Cheaper Option Grows" - XSEED Reckons Game-Key Cards Are Here To Stay
item.description:
"The end of physical media was declared many years ago".

Amongst the Switch 2's many Game-Key Card physical releases in its first year, Marvelous USA/XSEED has stood firm as one of the few third-party publishers consistently offering complete-on-card releases. Nintendo's new smaller cart option may entice more studios to follow suit, but XSEED CEO Ken Berry can't see the format going away any time soon.

In a new RPG Site interview all about the state of physical media in 2026, Berry admitted that it's actually "getting harder" for publishers to bring 'proper' physical releases to Switch 2, as GKCs are "getting more and more accepted," leading to a growing "pressure to go for the cheaper option".

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: GDC Survey Suggests Devs Want To Make Games For Switch 2 More Than PS5 Or Xbox
item.description:
Haw-haw!

The GDC Festival of Gaming has published its latest 'State of the Game Industry' report, which is based on a survey of over 2,600 game industry professionals on topics such as AI, layoffs, labour, and more.

One particular result caught our eye, and it's regarding which platforms developers are currently interested in developing for in the future. As expected, PC was comfortably the winner at 81%, likely down to its versatility, ease-of-use, and broad visibility of storefronts like Steam and Epic Games Store.

Try out some 2026 hits.

item.title: Review: TANUKI: Pon's Summer (Switch 2) - Cosy Postie Delivers Sick BMX Tricks & Minigames
item.description:
Ponhomie.

The gaming calendar is busier than it’s been in recent memory. We’re wedged between the Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6, having only just recovered from the onslaught of games that launched in September. The prospect of picking up another right now might not be an inviting one, but if any game could do it, it’s Tanuki: Pon’s Summer.

This quiet, cosy, understated gem has really launched at the perfect time. Playing as the titular Tanuki, you’re tasked with getting a shrine ready for a big festival towards the end of the summer. You have to raise funds for repair work, and find folks in town who can actually carry it out. To do so, you pick up a delivery job, get to know all of your eccentric neighbours, and pull off some sick BMX tricks along the way.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: "I Don't Feel This Is A Good Direction" - Chrono Trigger Composer Thinks It's Time To End Dragon Quest
item.description:

As covered by our pals over at Time Extension, Mitsuda-san believes that without Akira Toriyama – who sadly passed away in 2024 – the Dragon Quest franchise cannot continue imitating the iconic artist's signature style.
